_note: AI-drafted Call to Worship — pending Wilson's curation.

registers.label: Spare
lines: Unless a grain of wheat falls and dies, it remains alone.
But if it dies, it bears much fruit.
The message of the cross is foolishness to the perishing.
To us who are being saved, it is the power of God.
In you, O Lord, we take refuge; you have held us from birth.
Do not be far from us, O Lord.
The hour has come; come, let us worship.
Do not be far from us, O Lord. Amen.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: Hold a single seed in your hand, hard and dry; it can stay whole and alone, or it can fall into the dark and break open.
Do not be far from us, O Lord.
The hour has come, he says, for the Son of Man to be glorified, and glory turns out to mean a seed dropped into the ground to die.
Do not be far from us, O Lord.
The cross looks like foolishness to those who are perishing, like weakness, like loss; but it is the power and wisdom of God.
Do not be far from us, O Lord.
From the womb you called your servant, named us before we drew breath; from our youth you have been our refuge.
Do not be far from us, O Lord.
And I, when I am lifted up, will draw all people to myself. Come, let us worship and be drawn.
Do not be far from us, O Lord. Amen.

registers.label: Hybrid
lines: A grain of wheat must fall and die to bear its fruit.
Do not be far from us, O Lord.
The cross is foolishness to some, but to us the power of God.
Do not be far from us, O Lord.
From our youth you have been our refuge and our rock.
Do not be far from us, O Lord.
The hour has come. Come, let us worship.
Do not be far from us, O Lord. Amen.
